faq.q: How many times a day should a dog poop?
faq.a: Most adult dogs poop once or twice a day, according to the AKC, and dogs on higher-fiber diets may go about three times. What matters most is a change from your dog's usual pattern.

faq.q: How often should a puppy poop?
faq.a: More often than an adult, usually after each meal. Puppies tend to poop within about 30 minutes of eating, so with three or four meals a day several poops are normal.

faq.q: How long can a dog go without pooping before I should worry?
faq.a: The AKC says more than 24 to 36 hours is a cause for concern, and VCA advises calling your vet after 48 to 72 hours. If your dog is straining, vomiting or has a painful belly, go to the vet right away.

faq.q: Is it normal for my dog to poop only once a day?
faq.a: Yes. VCA notes most dogs poop at least once a day. Once a day is fine as long as the stool is firm and your dog is eating and acting normally.

faq.q: What can I give my dog for constipation?
faq.a: Check with your vet first. For mild cases vets often suggest more water, a consistent diet and fiber such as plain pumpkin or psyllium. Do not give human laxatives without your vet's advice.
